title: Illuminated Orbital Shaker for Microalgae Culture
author: Jakub Nedbal
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdubi6sn

steps.title: Procure required components
steps.instruction: Order all parts needed to build the illuminated orbital shaker from the indicated suppliers.

substeps.instruction: Orbital shaker (e.g., purchased on eBay).
Electronics components and mechanical fixings from an electronics distributor (e.g., Farnell).
Custom printed circuit board (PCB) from a PCB manufacturer (e.g., Seeed Technology).
Clear acrylic sheet from a specialist plastic supplier or a laser‑cut service.
3‑D‑printing service or in‑house printer (e.g., Stratasys Uprint SE Plus) for the controller case.
LED strips, heatsink, small cooling fans, metal stand‑offs, anti‑slip silicone mat, 24‑hour timer, and any required connectors.

steps.title: Assemble LED controller PCB
steps.instruction: Solder the surface‑mount components (0603 package) onto the LED controller PCB, test the circuit, clean excess flux, and follow all soldering safety precautions.

substeps.instruction: Gather soldering station, flux, watch‑maker tweezers, and fume extractor.
Place 0603 components on the PCB and solder; total soldering time should not exceed 1–2 hours.
Observe safety: keep work area free of combustibles, never leave the hot iron unattended, wear laboratory gloves when handling flux‑stained PCB, and use the fume extractor.
After soldering, test the LED controller circuit for correct operation.
Clean any remaining flux from the board.

steps.title: Print LED controller case
steps.instruction: Produce the custom case that houses the LED controller electronics using a fused‑deposition modeling printer or outsource the print; note that laser‑sintering yields a finer finish.

substeps.instruction: Load the case design into the printer software.
Print the case on a Stratasys Uprint SE Plus (or equivalent FDM printer).
If higher surface quality is desired, consider a laser‑sintering service.

steps.title: Build cooled LED illuminator
steps.instruction: Attach LED strips and cooling fans to the heatsink, glue them in place, solder the strips in a daisy‑chain, and wire the fans to the LED controller.

substeps.instruction: Apply adhesive to the underside of the heatsink and press the LED strips onto it.
Solder the LED strips together in a daisy‑chain configuration for power from the controller.
Glue the small fans onto the heatsink in positions that provide active cooling when LED current is high.
Connect the fan wires to the LED controller outputs.
Note: at low LED current the heatsink cools passively; at higher current the fans provide active cooling to prevent algal‑culture overheating.

steps.title: Cut and drill acrylic platform
steps.instruction: Shape the clear acrylic sheet to the required dimensions and drill mounting holes using a hacksaw and drill or a laser cutter.

substeps.instruction: Measure and mark the desired outline on the acrylic sheet.
Cut the sheet with a hacksaw (or use a laser cutter for a cleaner edge).
Drill holes for the metal stand‑offs and any other mounting features.

steps.title: Assemble illuminated orbital shaker
steps.instruction: Combine all sub‑assemblies to create the functional shaker, connect power, program the timer, and start the system.

substeps.instruction: Mount the acrylic platform on the orbital shaker using metal stand‑offs.
Place the cooled LED illuminator beneath the acrylic sheet.
Lay the supplied anti‑slip silicone mat on top of the acrylic.
Connect the LED controller to a power socket through a 24‑hour timer; program the timer for the desired day/night cycle.
Power on the system; verify that the shaker operates and the LEDs illuminate as intended.
